title: Prakrama 2, Sarga 1. The Manifestation of Ecstasy
html:
Opening of the second prakrama: Damodara Pandita asks to hear of the Lord's pastimes in Navadvipa; Murari's prayers; Shachi asks her Son for prema; the Lord's ecstatic states in Navadvipa

Verse 1

ततः प्रोवाच तच्छ्रुत्वा श्रीदामोदरपण्डितः।
नवद्वीपे किमकरोल्लीलां लीलानिधिः प्रभुः॥१॥

tataḥ provāca tacchrutvā śrīdāmodarapaṇḍitaḥ|
navadvīpe kimakarollīlāṁ līlānidhiḥ prabhuḥ||1||

tatah — then; provacha — said; tat — that; shrutva — having heard; shri-damodara-panditah — Sri Damodara Pandita; navadvipe — in Navadvipa; kim — what; akarot — performed; lilam — pastimes; lila-nidhih — the treasury of pastimes; prabhuh — the Lord.

1Having heard this, Sri Damodara Pandita1 said: "What pastimes did the Lord, the treasury of pastimes, perform in Navadvipa?

Verse 2

विस्तरेण वदस्वाद्य सर्वश्रुतिरसायनम्।
ततोऽसौ वक्तुमारेभे मुरारिर्हर्षयन्द्विजम्॥२॥

vistareṇa vadasvādya sarvaśrutirasāyanam|
tato'sau vaktumārebhe murārirharṣayandvijam||2||

vistarena — in detail; vadasva — tell; adya — now; sarva-shruti-rasayanam — an elixir for every ear; tatah — then; asau — he; vaktum — to speak; arebhe — began; murarih — Murari; harshayan — delighting; dvijam — the brahmana.

2Tell of them now in detail — it is an elixir for every ear." And then Murari, delighting the brahmana, began to speak:

Verse 3

श्रूयतां महदाश्चर्या कथा संक्षेपतो मम।
नत्वा वक्ष्यामि देवेशचैतन्यचरणाम्बुजम्॥३॥

śrūyatāṁ mahadāścaryā kathā saṁkṣepato mama|
natvā vakṣyāmi deveśacaitanyacaraṇāmbujam||3||

shruyatam — let it be heard; mahat-ashcharya — greatly wondrous; katha — the story; sankshepatah — in brief; mama — my; natva — having bowed; vakshyami — I shall tell; devesha-chaitanya-charana-ambujam — to the lotus feet of Chaitanya, Lord of the gods.

3"Hear my brief account, great and wondrous. Having bowed to the lotus feet of Chaitanya, Lord of the gods, I shall begin."

Verse 4

चैतन्यचन्द्र तव पादनखेन्दुकान्ति-
रेकादशेन्द्रियगणैः सहजीवकोषम्।
अन्तर्बहिश्च परिपूरय तस्य नित्यं
पुष्णातु नन्दयतु मे शरणागतस्य॥४॥

caitanyacandra tava pādanakhendukānti-
rekādaśendriyagaṇaiḥ sahajīvakoṣam|
antarbahiśca paripūraya tasya nityaṁ
puṣṇātu nandayatu me śaraṇāgatasya||4||

chaitanya-chandra — O Chaitanya-chandra; tava — of Your; pada-nakha-indu-kantih — the radiance of the moons of the toenails; ekadasha-indriya-ganaih saha — together with the host of eleven senses; jiva-kosham — the sheath of the soul; antah — within; bahih — without; cha — and; paripuraya — fill; tasya — of him; nityam — always; pushnatu — may it nourish; nandayatu — may it gladden; me — me; sharana-agatasya — who has taken refuge.

4O Chaitanya-chandra! Let the radiance of the moons of Your toenails fill the sheath of the soul together with its host of eleven senses2 — fill it within and without — and may it ever nourish and gladden me, who have taken refuge in You.

Verse 5

चैतन्यचन्द्र तव पादसरोजयुग्मं
दृष्ट्वापि ये त्वयि विभो न परेशबुद्धिम्।
कुर्वन्ति मोहवशगा रसभावहीना-
स्ते मोहिता विततवैभवमायया ते॥५॥

caitanyacandra tava pādasarojayugmaṁ
dṛṣṭvāpi ye tvayi vibho na pareśabuddhim|
kurvanti mohavaśagā rasabhāvahīnā-
ste mohitā vitatavaibhavamāyayā te||5||

chaitanya-chandra — O Chaitanya-chandra; tava — Your; pada-saroja-yugmam — pair of lotus feet; drishtva api — even having seen; ye — those who; tvayi — in You; vibho — O Almighty; na — not; paresha-buddhim — the thought of the Supreme Lord; kurvanti — hold; moha-vashagah — subject to delusion; rasa-bhava-hinah — devoid of rasa and feeling; te — they; mohitah — are deluded; vitata-vaibhava-mayaya — by the far-spread, mighty maya; te — Your.

5O Chaitanya-chandra! Those who, even after seeing Your lotus feet, do not recognize You, O Almighty, as the Supreme Lord — slaves of delusion, devoid of rasa and feeling — are deluded by Your far-spread and mighty maya.

Verse 6

चैतन्यचन्द्र न हि ते विबुधा विदन्ति
पादारविन्दयुगलं कुत एव चान्ये।
येषां मुकुन्द दयसे करुणार्द्रमूर्ते
ते त्वां भजन्ति प्रणमन्ति विदन्ति नित्यम्॥६॥

caitanyacandra na hi te vibudhā vidanti
pādāravindayugalaṁ kuta eva cānye|
yeṣāṁ mukunda dayase karuṇārdramūrte
te tvāṁ bhajanti praṇamanti vidanti nityam||6||

chaitanya-chandra — O Chaitanya-chandra; na hi — not at all; te — Your; vibudhah — the gods; vidanti — know; pada-aravinda-yugalam — pair of lotus feet; kutah eva — how then; cha — and; anye — others; yesham — to whom; mukunda — O Mukunda; dayase — You are merciful; karuna-ardra-murte — O You whose form is moist with compassion; te — they; tvam — You; bhajanti — worship; pranamanti — bow down; vidanti — know; nityam — always.

6O Chaitanya-chandra! Even the gods do not know Your lotus feet — how then could others? But those to whom You show mercy, O Mukunda, whose form is moist with compassion, worship You, bow to You and know You always.

Verse 7

नत्वा वदामि तव पादसहस्रपत्र-
माज्ञा विभो भवतु ते मम तत्र शक्तिः।
भूयाद्यथा तव कथामृतसारपूर्णा
वाणी वरेण्य नृहरे करुणामृताब्धे॥७॥

natvā vadāmi tava pādasahasrapatra-
mājñā vibho bhavatu te mama tatra śaktiḥ|
bhūyādyathā tava kathāmṛtasārapūrṇā
vāṇī vareṇya nṛhare karuṇāmṛtābdhe||7||

natva — having bowed; vadami — I speak; tava — to Your; pada-sahasrapatram — thousand-petalled lotus of the feet; ajna — the command; vibho — O Almighty; bhavatu — may be; te — Your; mama — my; tatra — therein; shaktih — strength; bhuyat — may become; yatha — so that; tava — of Your; katha-amrita-sara-purna — full of the essence of the nectar of the stories; vani — speech; varenya — O Most Excellent; nrihare — O Nrihari; karuna-amrita-abdhe — O ocean of the nectar of compassion.

7Bowing to the thousand-petalled lotus of Your feet, I say: O Almighty, let Your command be my strength in this task, so that my speech may be filled with the essence of the nectar of Your stories, O Most Excellent, O Nrihari, O ocean of the nectar of compassion!

Verse 8

आगत्य स्वगृहे कृष्णो हरिः प्रेमाश्रुलोचनः।
स्वगृहे पाठयन्नित्यं ब्राह्मणान्करुणानिधिः॥८॥

āgatya svagṛhe kṛṣṇo hariḥ premāśrulocanaḥ|
svagṛhe pāṭhayannityaṁ brāhmaṇānkaruṇānidhiḥ||8||

agatya — having come; sva-grihe — to His home; krishnah harih — Krishna Hari; prema-ashru-lochanah — His eyes full of tears of love; sva-grihe — in His home; pathayat — taught; nityam — daily; brahmanan — the brahmanas; karuna-nidhih — the treasury of compassion.

8Having returned home, Krishna Hari, the treasury of compassion, His eyes full of tears of love, taught the brahmanas in His house every day.

Verse 9

एकदा स्वगृहे सुप्तं रुदन्तं स्वसुतं शची।
प्रोवाच विस्मिता साध्वी किमिदं त्वं विरोदिषि॥९॥

ekadā svagṛhe suptaṁ rudantaṁ svasutaṁ śacī|
provāca vismitā sādhvī kimidaṁ tvaṁ virodiṣi||9||

ekada — once; sva-grihe — at home; suptam — sleeping; rudantam — weeping; sva-sutam — to her son; shachi — Shachi; provacha — said; vismita — astonished; sadhvi — the saintly; kim idam — what is this; tvam — you; virodishi — are weeping.

9One day the saintly Shachi, seeing her son weeping in His sleep, asked in astonishment: "What is this? Why are You weeping?"

Verse 10

नोवाच किञ्चित्तच्छ्रुत्वा मातरं प्रेमविह्वलः।
श्रीमद्विश्वम्भरो नाथस्तदासौ चिन्तिताभवत्॥१०॥

novāca kiñcittacchrutvā mātaraṁ premavihvalaḥ|
śrīmadviśvambharo nāthastadāsau cintitābhavat||10||

na uvacha — did not say; kinchit — anything; tat — that; shrutva — having heard; mataram — to His mother; prema-vihvalah — overwhelmed by love; shrimad-vishvambharah — Sriman Vishvambhara; nathah — the Lord; tada — then; asau — she; chintita — anxious; abhavat — became.

10Sriman Vishvambhara, the Lord, overwhelmed by love, heard this but said nothing to His mother, and she grew anxious.

Verse 11

हरेरनुग्रहात्काले ज्ञात्वा सा प्रेमलक्षणम्।
भक्तिं ययाचे गोविन्दे तां शची विनयान्विता॥११॥

hareranugrahātkāle jñātvā sā premalakṣaṇam|
bhaktiṁ yayāce govinde tāṁ śacī vinayānvitā||11||

hareh — of Hari; anugrahat — by the mercy; kale — in time; jnatva — having understood; sa — she; prema-lakshanam — the signs of love; bhaktim — devotion; yayache — begged; govinde — for Govinda; tam — that; shachi — Shachi; vinaya-anvita — humbly.

11In time, by Hari's mercy, she recognized the signs of prema and humbly begged Him for that devotion to Govinda:

Verse 12

यत्र तत्र धनं प्राप्य मह्यं तद्दत्तवान्भवान्।
प्रेमाख्यं किं धनं लब्धं गयायां देवदुर्लभम्॥१२॥

yatra tatra dhanaṁ prāpya mahyaṁ taddattavānbhavān|
premākhyaṁ kiṁ dhanaṁ labdhaṁ gayāyāṁ devadurlabham||12||

yatra tatra — wherever; dhanam — wealth; prapya — having gained; mahyam — to me; tat — it; dattavan — gave; bhavan — you; prema-akhyam — called prema; kim — what; dhanam — wealth; labdham — has been gained; gayayam — in Gaya; deva-durlabham — rare even for the gods.

12"Whatever wealth You have gained, wherever it was, You have always given it to me. What then is this wealth called prema, rare even for the gods, that You have gained in Gaya?

Verse 13

तन्मां प्रयच्छ ताताद्य यद्यस्ति करुणा मयि।
यथा कृष्णरसाम्भोधौ विहरामि निरन्तरम्॥१३॥

tanmāṁ prayaccha tātādya yadyasti karuṇā mayi|
yathā kṛṣṇarasāmbhodhau viharāmi nirantaram||13||

tat — that; mam — to me; prayachchha — give; tata — dear son; adya — today; yadi — if; asti — there is; karuna — compassion; mayi — for me; yatha — so that; krishna-rasa-ambhodhau — in the ocean of the rasa of Krishna; viharami — I may sport; nirantaram — unceasingly.

13Give it to me today, dear son, if You have any pity for me, so that I may sport unceasingly in the ocean of Krishna's rasa."

Verse 14

इति तस्या वचः श्रुत्वा मातुः स्नेहादुवाच ताम्।
वैष्णवानुग्रहान्मातस्तव तत्सम्भविष्यति॥१४॥

iti tasyā vacaḥ śrutvā mātuḥ snehāduvāca tām|
vaiṣṇavānugrahānmātastava tatsambhaviṣyati||14||

iti — thus; tasyah — her; vachah — words; shrutva — having heard; matuh — for His mother; snehat — out of affection; uvacha — said; tam — to her; vaishnava-anugrahat — by the mercy of the Vaishnavas; matah — O mother; tava — for you; tat — that; sambhavishyati — will come to be.

14Hearing these words, He answered His mother with affection: "Mother, by the mercy of the Vaishnavas this will come to be for you."

Verse 15

तच्छ्रुत्वा हर्षिता साध्वी भक्तियुक्ता बभूव सा।
श्रीमच्चैतन्यदेवोऽपि ब्राह्मणान्प्राह सादरम्॥१५॥

tacchrutvā harṣitā sādhvī bhaktiyuktā babhūva sā|
śrīmaccaitanyadevo'pi brāhmaṇānprāha sādaram||15||

tat — that; shrutva — having heard; harshita — delighted; sadhvi — the saintly lady; bhakti-yukta — filled with devotion; babhuva — became; sa — she; shrimach-chaitanya-devah — Sri Chaitanya-deva; api — and; brahmanan — to the brahmanas; praha — said; sadaram — respectfully.

15Hearing this, the saintly Shachi was delighted and became filled with devotion. And Sri Chaitanya-deva respectfully said to the brahmanas:

Verse 16

मात्रा मे प्रार्थितः प्रेमा हरौ तच्चावधीयताम्।
अस्मिन्यथा सा लभते हरिभक्तिं सुदुर्लभाम्॥१६॥

mātrā me prārthitaḥ premā harau taccāvadhīyatām|
asminyathā sā labhate haribhaktiṁ sudurlabhām||16||

matra — by My mother; me — from Me; prarthitah — has been asked; prema — love; harau — for Hari; tat — that; cha — and; avadhiyatam — let it be attended to; asmin — in this; yatha — how; sa — she; labhate — may obtain; hari-bhaktim — devotion to Hari; sudurlabham — most rare.

16"My mother has asked Me for love of Hari. Consider, then, how she may obtain this most rare devotion to Hari."

Verse 17

तच्छ्रुत्वोचुश्च ते सर्वे भविष्यति तवोदिता।
भक्तिस्तस्या जगन्नाथे प्रेमाख्या मुनिदुर्लभा॥१७॥

tacchrutvocuśca te sarve bhaviṣyati tavoditā|
bhaktistasyā jagannāthe premākhyā munidurlabhā||17||

tat — that; shrutva — having heard; uchuh — said; cha — and; te — they; sarve — all; bhavishyati — will be; tava — by You; udita — spoken of; bhaktih — the devotion; tasyah — hers; jagannathe — to the Lord of the world; prema-akhya — called prema; muni-durlabha — rare even for sages.

17Hearing this, they all said: "She will have that devotion to the Lord of the world of which You speak — the devotion called prema, rare even for sages."

Verse 18

तच्छ्रुत्वा श्रीशचीदेवी साक्षाद्भक्तिस्वरूपिणी।
लब्ध्वा हरौ दृढां भक्तिं प्रेमपूर्णा बभूव ह॥१८॥

tacchrutvā śrīśacīdevī sākṣādbhaktisvarūpiṇī|
labdhvā harau dṛḍhāṁ bhaktiṁ premapūrṇā babhūva ha||18||

tat — that; shrutva — having heard; shri-shachi-devi — Sri Shachi-devi; sakshat — manifestly; bhakti-svarupini — devotion personified; labdhva — having obtained; harau — for Hari; dridham — firm; bhaktim — devotion; prema-purna — full of love; babhuva — became; ha — indeed.

18Hearing this, Sri Shachi-devi — devotion personified — obtained firm devotion to Hari and became full of love.

Verse 19

ततो रोदिति स क्वापि नानाधारापरिप्लुतः।
नासे च श्लेष्मधाराभ्यां विप्लुते संबभूवतुः॥१९॥

tato roditi sa kvāpi nānādhārāpariplutaḥ|
nāse ca śleṣmadhārābhyāṁ viplute saṁbabhūvatuḥ||19||

tatah — then; roditi — weeps; sah — He; kvapi — at times; nana-dhara-pariplutah — bathed in many streams (of tears); nase — the nostrils; cha — and; shleshma-dharabhyam — with two streams of mucus; viplute — flooded; sambabhuvatuh — became.

19And from then on He would at times weep, bathed in many streams of tears, and both His nostrils were flooded by two streams of mucus.

Verse 20

विलुठन्भूतले देवः शुक्लाम्बरद्विजाश्रमे।
निरन्तरं श्लेष्मधारामाकृष्याकृष्य दूरतः॥२०॥

viluṭhanbhūtale devaḥ śuklāmbaradvijāśrame|
nirantaraṁ śleṣmadhārāmākṛṣyākṛṣya dūrataḥ||20||

viluthan — rolling; bhu-tale — on the ground; devah — the Lord; shuklambara-dvija-ashrame — in the hermitage of the brahmana Shuklambara; nirantaram — incessantly; shleshma-dharam — the stream of mucus; akrishya akrishya — drawing away again and again; duratah — far off.

20When the Lord rolled on the ground in the hermitage of the brahmana Shuklambara, the ceaseless stream of mucus was drawn away again and again

Verse 21

शुक्लाम्बरब्रह्मचारी क्षिपत्यनिशमेव हि।
गौरचन्द्रे रसेनापि परिपूर्णः सदा शुचिः॥२१॥

śuklāmbarabrahmacārī kṣipatyaniśameva hi|
gauracandre rasenāpi paripūrṇaḥ sadā śuciḥ||21||

shuklambara-brahmachari — Shuklambara Brahmachari; kshipati — throws; anisham — ceaselessly; eva hi — indeed; gaura-chandre — for Gaurachandra; rasena — with rasa; api — also; paripurnah — filled; sada — ever; shuchih — pure.

21and tirelessly thrown far off by Shuklambara Brahmachari — ever pure, and full of the rasa of love for Gaurachandra3.

Verse 22

रोदिति स दिनं प्राप्य प्रबुध्य रजनीमुखे।
दिवसोऽयमिति प्राह जना ऊचुरियं क्षपा॥२२॥

roditi sa dinaṁ prāpya prabudhya rajanīmukhe|
divaso'yamiti prāha janā ūcuriyaṁ kṣapā||22||

roditi — weeps; sah — He; dinam — the day; prapya — spending; prabudhya — awakening; rajani-mukhe — at nightfall; divasah — day; ayam — this; iti — thus; praha — says; janah — people; uchuh — said; iyam — this; kshapa — night.

22He would weep all day, and on waking at nightfall would say: "It is day." People would answer: "It is night."

Verse 23

एवं रजन्यां प्रेमार्द्रः सर्वां रात्रिं प्ररोदिति।
प्रहरैकं दिवा याते ततोऽसौ बुबुधे हरिः॥२३॥

evaṁ rajanyāṁ premārdraḥ sarvāṁ rātriṁ praroditi|
praharaikaṁ divā yāte tato'sau bubudhe hariḥ||23||

evam — thus; rajanyam — at night; prema-ardrah — melted with love; sarvam ratrim — the whole night; proroditi — weeps profusely; prahara-ekam — by one prahara; diva — the day; yate — having gone; tatah — then; asau — He; bubudhe — awoke; harih — Hari.

23So, melted by love, He would weep aloud the whole night through, and only when the first prahara4 of the day had passed did Hari come to Himself.

Verse 24

ततः प्राह कियद्रात्रिर्वर्तते प्राह तं जनः।
दिवसोऽयमतिप्रेम्णा न जानाति दिनं क्षपाम्॥२४॥

tataḥ prāha kiyadrātrirvartate prāha taṁ janaḥ|
divaso'yamatipremṇā na jānāti dinaṁ kṣapām||24||

tatah — then; praha — says; kiyat — how much; ratrih — of the night; vartate — remains; praha — says; tam — to Him; janah — a person; divasah — day; ayam — this; ati-premna — through excess of love; na janati — He does not know; dinam — day; kshapam — night.

24Then He would ask: "How much of the night is left?" and someone would answer: "It is day." Through excess of love He could not tell day from night.

Verse 25

क्वचिच्छ्रुत्वा हरेर्नाम गीतं वा विह्वलः क्षितौ।
पतति श्रुतिमात्रेण दण्डवत्कम्पते क्वचित्॥२५॥

kvacicchrutvā harernāma gītaṁ vā vihvalaḥ kṣitau|
patati śrutimātreṇa daṇḍavatkampate kvacit||25||

kvachit — sometimes; shrutva — having heard; hareh — of Hari; nama — the name; gitam — a song; va — or; vihvalah — overwhelmed; kshitau — on the ground; patati — falls; shruti-matrena — merely by hearing; dandavat — like a stick; kampate — trembles; kvachit — sometimes.

25Sometimes, hearing the name of Hari or a song about Him, He was overwhelmed and at the mere sound fell to the ground like a stick; sometimes He trembled.

✦

Notes

  1. The poem is framed as a dialogue: Murari Gupta tells Damodara Pandita of the Lord's life. "This" is the account of the first prakrama, which ended with the Lord's return from Gaya.
  2. The eleven senses are the five organs of knowledge, the five organs of action, and the mind.
  3. Shuklambara Brahmachari was a poor brahmana of Navadvipa who lived on alms; one of the Lord's first companions.
  4. A prahara ("watch") is an eighth part of the day and night, about three hours.
